answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a vertex’s influence is weighted by paths that repeatedly encounter independent attestations rather than by self-created identities. A Sybil cluster S with a sparse external cut has low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), and few walks escape it; min-cut transitivity bounds therefore limit how much external trust it can import and cap its aggregate voting weight. A ridge in this trust landscape marks the bottleneck; copper-colored labels would not change the bound.
